plan: Store the input dictionary deep-copied in the Workspace; to_data() returns another deep copy so callers can never alias internal state.

Implement one recursive depth-first generator over items that descends into section/group containers; use it for word counting, marker collection, and id lookup so all operations treat every nesting level uniformly.
total_word_count(): for notes, remove [[?identifier]] marker tokens (replaced with a space) then count \b\w+\b runs; for references, add the declared word_count.
unresolved_markers(): collect identifiers from note-text markers plus each reference's unresolved list into a set, return sorted list.
outline(): emit the workspace title, then recurse over items appending '  ' * level + '<kind>: <title>', with top-level items at level 1.

move(): validate everything before mutating — item_id/destination_id are strings, item exists, destination is the literal 'workspace' or an existing section/group, destination is not the moved item nor any of its descendants, and index (when given) is an int in [0, len(destination items)]. Only then pop the item from its parent list and insert/append into the destination, so any ValueError leaves the workspace untouched and a success moves the intact subtree.
mechanisms: Recursive part–whole tree of dict nodes with section/group as containers
Single shared depth-first generator applied uniformly across levels
Recursive aggregation for word totals and marker sets
Deterministic pre-order traversal for indented outline rendering
Containment/no-cycle validation (container destinations only, no self- or descendant-destination)
Atomic move: full validation before any mutation, then pop-and-insert of the intact subtree
Deep-copy isolation at construction and in to_data()
